description: APP HEALTH: the orders-api process serves /healthz (and /readyz) but has NO /health route — so a probe pointed at /health gets a 404, not because the app is down
command: grep -Eq '@router.get\("/healthz"\)' app/orders-api/src/health.py && ! grep -Eq '@router.get\("/health"\)' app/orders-api/src/health.py && echo pass || echo fail

description: PROBE CONFIG: the RENDERED readiness probe points at /health — the path the app does not serve — so the pod will never report Ready
command: helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api 2>/dev/null | grep -A2 readinessProbe | grep -Eq 'path: /health$' && echo pass || echo fail

description: PROBE CONFIG: the liveness probe correctly points at /healthz — this is the misleading part, the container is NOT killed, it just stays perpetually unready
command: helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api 2>/dev/null | grep -A2 livenessProbe | grep -Eq 'path: /healthz$' && echo pass || echo fail

description: ROLLOUT STATE: maxUnavailable is rendered as 100% — a rolling update may take every old pod down before a new one is Ready, turning an unready rollout into a full outage
command: helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api 2>/dev/null | grep -Eq 'maxUnavailable: 100%' && echo pass || echo fail

description: THE FIX: the defect lives in Helm values (desired state in Git), not in the app or the cluster — so the repair is a one-line values change routed through the reconciler, not a kubectl edit
command: grep -Eq 'path: /health\b' platform/helm/orders-api/values.yaml && echo pass || echo fail

description: THE FIX VERIFIED: overriding the readiness path to /healthz renders a probe that matches the app's real endpoint (proven with helm template and a values override, no cluster touched)
command:
f=$(mktemp); printf 'readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: http
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
' > "$f"; helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api -f "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -A2 readinessProbe | grep -Eq 'path: /healthz$' && echo pass || echo fail; rm -f "$f"

description: GOVERNANCE: the repair path is the golden path — a direct kubectl edit of the live deployment from an agent identity is exactly the wrong-target class the gate blocks; the fix is proposed in Git
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"kubectl edit deployment orders-api -A"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail
